short: An unlikely emperor, installed by the Praetorian Guard, who governed with more competence than his family expected.
full:
Claudius, Caligula's uncle, had been sidelined for life by a physical disability his family took for stupidity. When the Praetorian Guard found him hiding after Caligula's murder, they proclaimed him emperor on 24 January 41 CE and presented the Senate with a fait accompli, the first time the throne had passed by military acclamation rather than senatorial or dynastic process.

Claudius proved a capable administrator, expanding the imperial bureaucracy, extending citizenship in the provinces, and beginning the conquest of Britain in 43 CE. His domestic life was less orderly: his fourth wife Agrippina the Younger is widely thought to have arranged his death by poison on 13 October 54 CE to clear the way for her son Nero, whom Claudius had adopted, over his own son Britannicus.
